Offline code worker gpt-6.1-sol xhigh per explicit user instruction. Workspace /home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela. Read root README/applicable AGENTS/xts-board-evidence skill. Root sole hardware/UART/USB/Windows/network/credential owner. Do not use any live board or host network/process inventory. No downloads/upgrades, baseline reruns, git switches/cleanup/push, mainline/frozen edits or subagents.

Implement the ONE next direction in backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-udp-append-disjoint-copy/first-board-review.md, reading its first-board-statistics.json and relevant code/cost review. E107 completed RX/TX/quiet and original is fully restored; product adoption HOLD. RX13.743128/TX8.869784 Mbit/s, actual host input16.403632, cap5210, residual8696 B unresolved. FixedE90 targets stay24.753333/12.133968. No causal memcpy gain demonstrated. We are not repeating an achieved rate or baseline.

Write ONLY a new backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-udp-consumer-observation/. Begin with selected-file staging and focused actual-function host validation, not whole source-tree copying or a whole-image build yet. Parent code is frozen E107 disjoint-copy source; retaining it as diagnostic parent is not product adoption. Deliver minimal source patch against pinned parent and staged changed files, test evidence, counter contract and memory/frame/clock cost design sufficient for Root/Astra review. Root will decide subsequent paired build and screen; no runnable hardware entrypoint now.

Exact gap: selected-port59441 recv consumer time acquiring conn_dev_lock, draining buffered readahead, and bounded call-to-call elapsed where backlog observed at endpoints. Sites psock_udp_recvfrom in nuttx/net/udp/udp_recvfrom.c, udp_readahead helper, and existing esp32s31_monstat/observer export. Distinguish immediate buffered/direct/empty wait and error paths. No claims of continuous backlog between endpoints, CPU load or total via x16 extrapolation. Sample using existing HR clock at bounded stride and fixed counters, preserve all actual I/O operations/return/errno/ownership/free/lock/wait/cancellation behavior. No new retained packet, tail cache, queue/buffer growth, scheduling policy or lock/cache/IRQ/checksum/security/timeout relaxation. New diagnostic state must have exact bounded cost and synchronization/lifecycle proof; invalidate ambiguity from concurrent/different consumers, socket lifecycle/pointer reuse, missing prior valid endpoint, clock/counter overflow. If call-to-call identity cannot be measured safely with a small bounded diagnostic change, explicitly leave that field unavailable and deliver lock/drain observations with the precise limitation; don't add a generic tracing subsystem or unsafe stale-pointer cache.

Existing append prefix494 bytes is stable, legacy reader tail has numeric corruption because it reformats partial reads. Do not parse legacy fields as coherent or silently treat them fixed. New consumer fields must have a bounded, fixed-width, independently valid prefix/format and an explicit exact chunked-read contract. Preserve prior append instrumentation semantics and raw history; cost of any prefix/state change must be measured. Do not broadly rewrite the device reader unless needed and justified. Root captures quiescent snapshots, not concurrent UART polling during traffic.

Use actual parent/candidate recv path with focused host fixtures, observation-on/off byte/metadata/peek/trunc/short/zero/error/cancellation semantics, lifecycle/concurrent invalidation, sample/phase/overflow conservation and chunked prefix parsing. Reuse existing relevant harnesses and completed copy tests without replaying unrelated suites. Tests should validate real behavior, not just assert implementation constants. Keep a small selected-input preservation manifest, source diff, schema, focused test log and reviewable README/receipt. Explain actual affected flags/config and RV32 state/alignment implications; target build/frame validation is deliberately pending. No new source-local throughput fix justified yet; observation-only. Don't alter E90, docs current matrix/checklist, FS staging/postcapture or runner frozen files. Stop once selected implementation is reviewable; promptly report concrete blockers rather than expanding scope.

I’ll read the repository guidance and pinned E107 review, then stage only the selected inputs in the new consumer-observation directory. I’ll validate the actual receive path with focused host fixtures and leave target builds and hardware entrypoints pending.

I’m applying the xts-board-evidence skill to preserve the frozen evidence and its acceptance limits. E107 remains a diagnostic parent with product adoption on HOLD; this work is limited to the receive-consumer observation gap.

The parent confirms that `conn_dev_lock` and `udp_readahead` are the missing timing boundaries. I’ll leave call-to-call timing explicitly unavailable: a safe identity across calls would need lifecycle tracking beyond this small change. The probe will retain no socket, task or packet pointer and will publish lock/drain observations before entering the cancellable wait.

The 30 selected inputs are staged. I’m validating the unmodified parent receive function first, including its zero-length behavior: on a blocking call, a zero result from readahead still enters the wait branch. The observation must preserve that behavior.

The parent fixture passed. To avoid reading port identity before acquiring the connection lock, the probe takes a ticket every sixteenth supported UDP receive call and checks port 59441 under the existing lock. The export records that sampling basis. It uses at most three HR clock reads per ticket and has no diagnostic lifetime extending across the wait.

The candidate now separates immediate buffered reads, empty nonblocking returns, wait entry/result, and callback-allocation failure. Lock/drain samples finish before wait entry, so cancellation needs no new cleanup hook. A concurrency test exposed a fixture bug—it destroyed a shared mutex before all fixture threads had joined. That is corrected, and validation is running again.

The parent, candidate, and disabled-observation profiles pass the focused ASan/UBSan checks with matching byte, metadata, return and operation digests. The new prefix is 744 bytes, following the unchanged 494-byte append prefix. Chunk tests preserve both while deliberately changing legacy fields between reads; the new parser will reject incomplete or invalid consumer prefixes and ignore the legacy tail.

I added a separate count for waits reached after a zero-result buffered drain, so they cannot be mistaken for waits that began empty. The final consumer block is 779 bytes; its accumulator and lock total 180 bytes. Call-to-call timing remains unconditionally unavailable. I’m sealing the patch, parser contract, host cost results and preservation receipt for review.

The final audit confirms two changed source files, 30 preserved inputs unchanged, and matching disabled-observer preprocessing. All eleven host profiles and eight chunk-size checks pass. Call-to-call timing is explicitly unavailable, and target compilation, frames, linked costs and hardware screening remain pending. I’m checking the sealed delivery hashes now.

Created the [review package](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-udp-consumer-observation/README.md), containing the two-file patch, staged sources, counter/prefix contracts, focused evidence and cost receipt.

- Eleven host profiles passed; 30 preserved inputs remain unchanged.
- New bounded state: 180 bytes before linker padding.
- Call-to-call timing remains explicitly unavailable.
- Target build/frame validation and hardware screening remain pending Root/Astra review. Adoption stays HOLD.

All writes are confined to the requested new directory.
